steps: Finely chop the onion, bell pepper, garlic and half the cilantro into a sofrito paste.
Rub the chicken thighs with the sofrito, the juice of the lime, oregano, cumin, adobo, culantro, salt and black pepper, and marinate at least 30 minutes.
Scrape the marinade off the chicken and reserve it. Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat, add the sugar, and let it melt and darken to a copper caramel.
Add the chicken to the caramelised sugar and brown 3-4 minutes per side until the pieces take on a deep mahogany colour.
Stir in the reserved sofrito and the tomato sauce, then add enough water to come halfway up the chicken, about three quarters of a cup.
Add the diced potato and carrot, cover, and simmer 25-30 minutes until the chicken and potato are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Scatter the remaining cilantro over the stew and serve.

note: Dominican rebuild: breast->thigh (braising cut), coconut milk and green beans dropped, carrot + cilantro added, sofrito marinade and the azucar quemada burnt-sugar step added; Adobo + Culantro spice overrides. Thigh raised 170->190 and potato trimmed 120->100 to hold calories flat against the breast->thigh protein loss.

steps: Finely chop the onion, bell pepper, garlic and half the cilantro into a sofrito.
Season the chicken thighs with half the sofrito plus cumin, oregano, culantro, salt and black pepper, and let them sit 15 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a caldero or heavy pot, brown the chicken 4 minutes per side, and remove it.
Add the remaining sofrito to the pot with the annatto and coriander powder and cook 3 minutes until the oil turns orange-gold.
Stir in the rice and tomato sauce so every grain is coated, then pour in about three quarters of a cup of chicken stock.
Nestle the chicken back into the rice, cover, and cook 20 minutes without stirring so a pegao crust forms on the bottom.
Scatter the green peas over the top, cover 2 more minutes, then fold through the remaining cilantro and rest 5 minutes before serving.

note: Puerto Rican rebuild: coconut milk and green beans removed, green peas 40->70 standing in for gandules, sofrito built at the start, sazon spelled out as Annatto + Coriander Powder, Culantro added, hard-coded 1.5 cups water rescaled to 3/4 cup stock for 55 g rice.

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions.
Mash the garlic with the adobo, oregano, cumin and black pepper into a paste and rub it over the flank steak. Marinate at least 30 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and sear the steak 3 minutes per side, then set it aside.
Add the sliced onion and bell pepper to the pot with the smoked paprika and cook 6-8 minutes until soft and sweet.
Deglaze with the white wine and let it reduce by half, then stir in the tomato sauce, the bay leaves and about 1 cup of water.
Return the steak to the pot, cover, and braise on low heat for 3 hours until it pulls apart with no resistance.
Remove the bay leaves and shred the beef with two forks directly in the sauce, then simmer uncovered 10-15 minutes to marry.
Season with salt, finish with the chopped cilantro, and serve over the rice with a wedge of lime.

note: Cuban rebuild: eggplant (phantom vegetable), soy sauce and the 0.5 g lemon removed; Beef Sirloin -> Flank Steak for the shredded texture; sofrito moved to the front of the braise; White Wine (registry row) replaces the soy sauce as vino seco; Bell Pepper 80->110, Cilantro + Lime added; Smoked Paprika added. Data-bug fix: the bogus Water spice-override entry is gone and the recipe now carries Salt and Black Pepper like every other savory dish.

recipe.name: Jerk Chicken with Rice and Peas

steps: Soak the kidney beans overnight, then drain and simmer them in about 1 cup of fresh water until tender, roughly 45 minutes.
Blend the green onion, garlic, ginger, serrano chile, allspice, thyme, cinnamon, soy sauce, honey and the juice of the lime into a thick wet paste.
Coat the chicken thighs in the paste, cover, and marinate at least 4 hours and ideally overnight.
Add the white rice and the coconut milk to the beans and their liquid, top up so the rice is just covered, cover the pot and cook 18-20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Grill or pan-sear the marinated chicken 6-7 minutes per side, letting the outside char - jerk should taste smoky.
Dice the bell pepper and onion and saute them briefly until just softened.
Rest the chicken, slice it against the grain, and serve over the rice and peas with the peppers and onion alongside.

note: Jamaican rebuild: dry rub -> real wet jerk paste (green onion, fresh garlic, ginger, chile, allspice, thyme, cinnamon, soy sauce, honey, lime) marinated overnight; Cayenne and Garlic Powder dropped; the invented coconut-milk drizzle replaced by proper rice and peas (kidney beans + coconut milk cooked into the rice). Renamed to what the fixed dish actually is. Rice trimmed 50->40 and coconut milk held at 50 g to cap the calorie rise at about +28% rather than the report's +200 cal.

steps: Soak the black beans overnight, then drain them.
Cut the pork belly and pork loin into cubes and season them with salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and brown the pork belly until its fat renders, then add the pork loin and brown that too.
Add most of the diced onion and the minced garlic and cook 3 minutes until softened, reserving a spoonful of onion for the farofa.

Add the drained beans, the bay leaves and about 1 cup of water, then simmer covered for 2-3 hours, adding more water as it reduces, until the liquor is dark and thick. Mash a ladle of beans against the side of the pot to thicken it.
Cook the white rice according to package directions.
For the farofa, melt half the butter in a skillet, soften the reserved onion, then stir in the cassava flour over low heat and toast it, stirring constantly, until it is golden and sandy.
For the couve, shred the kale into fine ribbons and flash-saute it in the remaining butter for 2 minutes so it stays bright green.
Remove the bay leaves and serve the beans over the rice with the farofa, the couve and slices of fresh orange alongside.

note: Rio-style rebuild: single lean Pork Loin -> Pork Belly + Pork Loin mix (fat and two textures, the report's own no-new-ingredient fallback for Linguica); beans 46->60 so the beans are the body; the three missing accompaniments added - farofa (Cassava Flour + Butter), couve (Kale) and sliced Orange; Lime removed (orange is the feijoada citrus); Cumin removed as a wrong-cuisine import and Bay Leaves added. Data-bug fix: hard-coded '2 cups' water rescaled to about 1 cup for 60 g dry beans, in step text only. Portions trimmed against the report's full weights to land at about +28% calories instead of +77%.

steps: Peel and devein the shrimp, then marinate them with the juice of the lime, the minced garlic and a good pinch of salt for 20 minutes.
Cook the white rice according to package directions.
Slice the onion, tomato and bell pepper into rounds rather than dicing them.
Layer the onion, tomato and bell pepper in the bottom of a heavy pot or clay panela with half the cilantro, and season with salt, black pepper and the cayenne.
Lay the marinated shrimp on top of the vegetables without stirring.
Pour the coconut milk and the palm oil over everything, cover, and cook gently 8-10 minutes until the shrimp turn pink. Do not stir and do not brown anything.
Scatter the remaining cilantro and the sliced green onion over the top and serve straight from the pot, spooning the broth over the rice.

note: Moqueca baiana rebuild: Palm Oil (Dende) added as the defining fat and Paprika removed (its only job was faking the dende colour); Olive Oil dropped since nothing is browned; Tomato Sauce 50 -> fresh Tomato 120 for the layered, brothy result; Cilantro and Garlic added; technique changed from saute-then-simmer to raw layering in a covered pot; lime moved into a shrimp marinade instead of a finishing squeeze. Green Onion added as the report's optional garnish.

steps: Cook the white rice and the black beans separately according to package directions.
Dice the tomato, the red onion and the bell pepper small for the vinagrete, dress them with the red wine vinegar, salt and black pepper, and let them sit 10 minutes.
Score the fat cap of the beef in a crosshatch and season it generously with coarse salt.
Sear the beef fat-side down first until the cap renders and browns deeply, then turn it and cook 3-4 minutes on the meat side for medium-rare. Rest it 5 minutes.

For the farofa, melt the butter in a skillet, soften the diced onion and the minced garlic, then stir in the cassava flour over low heat and toast it, stirring constantly, until it is golden and sandy. Season with salt.
Slice the steak against the grain and serve it with the rice, the beans, the farofa and a spoonful of vinagrete.

note: Data-bug fix plus rebuild: Cassava Flour added, so the dish named 'with Farofa' now contains farofa - the old step 4 sauteed onion and garlic in a dry pan and called that a 'farofa flavor base' with no flour anywhere. Butter added to toast it. Vinagrete added (Tomato, Red Onion, Bell Pepper, Red Wine Vinegar) as the real acidic partner, replacing the lone Lime squeeze which is removed. Egg dropped as non-traditional (that is bife a cavalo, not churrasco) which also offsets the added carbs. Steak steps rewritten for the fat-cap method. Salt-only seasoning on the steak kept, as the report credits.

_summary.notes: All 7 were significantly-off; all 7 rewritten. Calorie deltas vs current: Pollo Guisado ~flat (607->607), Arroz con Pollo -7% (756->703), Ropa Vieja +3% (779->805), Jerk +28% (543->695), Feijoada +28% (683->875), Moqueca +10% (616->677), Picanha +14% (708->808). Feijoada and Jerk were the two the report predicted would blow up (+350-450 and +200 respectively); I trimmed portions below the report's stated grams to land both near +28% rather than +77% and +39%, because SPEC caps drift at roughly +/-25%. If the validator still struggles, Feijoada is the one to shrink further - halve the Pork Belly again. Ingredients this slice stops using, none orphaned but worth the hygiene sweep: Coconut Milk (Pollo Guisado, Arroz con Pollo), Green Beans (both), Eggplant + Soy Sauce + Lemon (Ropa Vieja), Chicken Breast (Pollo Guisado), Tomato Sauce (Moqueca), Egg + Lime (Picanha), Lime (Feijoada), Pork Loin partly (Feijoada). Beef Sirloin loses one use to Flank Steak in Ropa Vieja; Flank Steak now has at least this one use and needs the MEAT_INGREDIENTS Set check, as do Pork Belly and Kidney Beans if they were not already added in Phase A. Per the standing rule, green olives and capers (traditional in pollo guisado, arroz con pollo and ropa vieja) and nutmeg (traditional in jerk) are deliberately absent everywhere - this is not an oversight.
